name: Hydroxychloroquine and related disease-modifying drugs
summary: MedlinePlus places hydroxychloroquine in a group of medicines called antimalarials and also describes it as an antirheumatic drug. The NHS describes it as a disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) that works by blocking the effects of chemicals released when the immune system attacks the body. The Royal College of Ophthalmologists publishes eye-monitoring recommendations for users of hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine.
mechanism: Reviews describe hydroxychloroquine building up in lysosomes and disrupting how immune cells process antigens, and one review notes that its exact mechanism has not been fully worked out.
cautions: Retinal damage from these medicines is largely irreversible, so eye monitoring is recommended.
The Royal College says extra risk factors can justify eye monitoring from the start of treatment, as decided by the prescriber.
The Royal College says chloroquine appears to be more retinotoxic than hydroxychloroquine.

classInteractions.effect: The Royal College lists tamoxifen use as a factor that can justify eye monitoring from the start of treatment.

source.title: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists: Hydroxychloroquine and Chloroquine Retinopathy: Recommendations on Monitoring

classWarnings.text: NRAS advises contacting the GP or specialist team about any change in vision.
